audit.whatIsWrong: The entry's whole plan is built on Relentless Pursuit being down — 'engage only when E dash is on cooldown', 'when it is down he has no escape', loading says 'Engage only on Relentless Pursuit's cooldown'. The one line in Riot's text that governs that window is never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot: 'Lightslinger attacks reduce Relentless Pursuit's cooldown.' The dash is 16/15.5/15/14.5/14, so a player who counts to sixteen and steps in is walking into a dash that came back early — because every empowered shot Lucian landed in the interim refunded part of it. The correct instruction is not to wait out a timer but to deny him Lightslinger attacks, which is a completely different behaviour: hold spacing after each of his ability casts rather than trading autos through them.
audit.corrected: Relentless Pursuit is 16s at rank 1, but Lightslinger attacks refund part of it — the window only exists if his empowered shots have been missing.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lucian.json (E Relentless Pursuit, cd 16/15.5/15/14.5/14, 'Lightslinger attacks reduce Relentless Pursuit's cooldown'; P Lightslinger)

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says 'R slows Lucian and telegraphs your all-in commitment' and whys[5] says 'the cast slows him and commits him to fighting inside your W'.
audit.why: Subjugate has no slow. Riot: 'Trundle immediately steals a percent of his target's Health, Armor and Magic Resistance. Over the next 4 seconds the amount stolen is doubled.' The slows in Trundle's kit are Chomp's brief one and Pillar of Ice's area slow. A player who casts R expecting it to hold Lucian in place will watch him dash out with the theft still ticking — and against a squishy target the stat steal is small, so the cast has bought nothing.
audit.corrected: Subjugate is a stat theft, not a hold. The slows are Chomp and Pillar of Ice — cut his exit with Pillar first, then spend R as commitment.
sources: champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (R Subjugate; Q and E carry the slow flags)

audit.whatIsWrong: early says 'his passive lets him fire two shots off every Q cast', and wants.foe[1] says 'Double-shot proc on every Q cast'. Ardent Blaze is never named anywhere in either layer, and Piercing Light's targeting is never described.
audit.why: Three gaps in one paragraph. Lightslinger triggers off ANY ability, not just Q — including Relentless Pursuit, so the dash out is itself an empowered shot. Piercing Light 'shoots a bolt of piercing light THROUGH a target' at 500 range, so a minion standing between you is not cover; he can cast it on the minion. And Ardent Blaze marks at 900 range and grants Lucian move speed for attacking marked enemies, which is the actual mechanic beating Frozen Domain's movement speed — the entry keeps saying he kites you without ever naming what he kites with.
audit.corrected: Lightslinger empowers his next attack after any ability, including the dash out. Piercing Light fires through its target at 500 range. Ardent Blaze marks at 900 and every auto into the mark gives him move speed.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lucian.json (P Lightslinger; Q Piercing Light range 500; W Ardent Blaze range 900, cd 14/13/12/11/10)

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[6] credits Chomp with an 'attack speed debuff'.
audit.why: Chomp saps Attack Damage and briefly slows movement. There is no attack-speed component anywhere in Trundle's kit — the attack speed is Frozen Domain's, and it is a buff on him, not a debuff on the enemy. Against Lucian the AD sap is the point, because his burst is attack-damage-driven, so naming it correctly makes the advice stronger, not weaker.
audit.corrected: Chomp saps his Attack Damage and briefly slows. The attack speed in this matchup is Frozen Domain's, on you.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither ultimate carries a cooldown. spikes[1] and whys[5] discuss the level-6 window purely in terms of how little Subjugate steals from a squishy target.
audit.why: The Culling is 110/100/90 and Subjugate is 120/100/80. They cross: at rank 1 his ultimate is back first by ten seconds, at rank 2 they are level, and at rank 3 yours is back first by ten. That is a real change in who can force the side lane as the game goes on, and it is the concrete reason the two-item stage tilts to Trundle.
audit.corrected: The Culling 110/100/90 against Subjugate 120/100/80 — his is up first at rank 1, level at rank 2, and yours is up first at rank 3.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagree about the opening. content early opens 'Levels 1-3 are Lucian's lane' and whys[0] through whys[2] all describe Trundle losing those stages, while full phases[0].why under the same stage says 'Chomp start — bite Lucian on every last-hit attempt. The flat damage plus AD steal wins almost every level-1 exchange.' The chart hands Trundle none of the seven stages in a lane the packet scores 52.79% over 430 games, and the full layer calls it FAV while report[14] calls it a 'Hard matchup'.
audit.why: Both stories cannot be true at Level 1. The content layer's version is the defensible one for this specific matchup — Lightslinger gives Lucian a double-shot off his first ability and Piercing Light outranges Chomp's 300 by 200 — so the generic full-layer 'Chomp bully' line is the one that is wrong here. The chart itself is defensible as Skill-heavy, but 430 games at 52.79% with none of seven stages to Trundle is hard to justify, and the two-item stage contradicts whys[6] and spikes[3], which both say Lucian falls off against your armour.
audit.corrected: Levels 1-3 are Lucian's on Lightslinger and Piercing Light's range. The two-item stage is Trundle's — win[6] and phases[6].side should read Trundle, matching spikes[3] and the 52.79% headline.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[10] says 'Your engage is premium gank setup — ping your jungler when Relentless Pursuit is down' with no caveat.
audit.why: Lightslinger's second clause matters here: 'when a nearby enemy Champion is immobilized, his next 2 basic attacks will deal bonus magic damage.' A jungler's stun or root therefore hands Lucian two empowered attacks in the middle of the gank. It does not make ganking wrong, but it means the CC has to land as the kill lands, not as the opener, and it explains why sloppy collapses on Lucian go badly.
audit.corrected: Hard CC from your jungler empowers Lucian's next two attacks with bonus magic damage — land the crowd control to finish the gank, not to start it.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are Lucian's lane. His passive lets him fire two shots off every Q cast, and at melee range he can proc the double-shot on your face before you land a Chomp. Do not walk into his Q range to start trades — you will absorb a double proc and a basic auto before your bite even resolves. Take Chomp first and stay back, last-hitting at max range. When he steps up to Q you, sidestep and punish with a single Chomp auto, then back off before the double-shot clips you. You cannot out-trade him in a short burst at these levels; your only edge is that King's Tribute heals you off every dead minion, so small chip damage recovers faster than he expects.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are Lucian's lane. Lightslinger turns his next attack into a double-shot after ANY ability, not only Q, so even his dash out arrives empowered. Piercing Light fires through its target at 500 range, so a minion between you is not cover. Do not walk in to start trades — you absorb a double proc and an auto before your bite resolves. Take Chomp first and last-hit at max range. When he steps up to Q, sidestep and punish with a single Chomp auto, then leave before the double-shot clips you. Your edge is King's Tribute healing you off every dead minion, so chip recovers faster than he expects.

edits.before: From levels 4-6 the lane becomes a read. Lucian wants short aggressive trades: Q in, double-shot, E away. You want the opposite — to lock him on your W and drag the fight to five or more autos where your Chomp AD steal and W healing tip the math. The key tool is Pillar: place it not where he is standing but where his E dash is going, cutting off the retreat. If you land that Pillar and he is inside Frozen Domain with his E burned, you win the extended trade even before level 6. At level 6, Subjugate gives limited resistance-drain value on a squishy ADC, but the real use is tempo — R slows Lucian and telegraphs your all-in commitment; layer it with Pillar-cut and a W drop immediately under your feet, and his only out is a dash you have already blocked.
edits.after: From levels 4-6 the lane becomes a read. Lucian wants short aggressive trades: Q in, double-shot, E away. You want the opposite — lock him on your W and drag the fight past five autos where the Chomp AD steal and W healing tip the math. The key tool is Pillar: place it where his E is going, not where he stands. But do not simply count to sixteen — Lightslinger attacks refund Relentless Pursuit's cooldown, so every empowered shot he lands buys his escape back early. Ardent Blaze is the other half: it marks you at 900 range and each auto into the mark gives him move speed, which is what beats Frozen Domain. At 6 Subjugate takes little off a squishy Lucian, so spend it as commitment behind a Pillar cut and a W under your feet.

edits.before: Two items is where this matchup settles in your favour. Iceborn Gauntlet's Spellblade procs on every Chomp and the zone it creates around you is a second Frozen Domain effect — Lucian simply cannot kite a Trundle who has both W and Gauntlet slow active simultaneously. His damage does not scale the way a true carry does; by mid-to-late game his burst window requires two full rotations to kill you, and inside that second rotation you have healed back a significant chunk. Split-push with W, bait his E onto a non-committal angle, drop Pillar to cut his escape, and finish with Chomp. In team fights save Subjugate for an enemy frontliner — do not waste R on Lucian when a tank is present.
edits.after: Two items is where this matchup settles in your favour. Iceborn Gauntlet's Spellblade procs off every Chomp and its chill stacks with Frozen Domain — Lucian struggles to kite a Trundle running both slows at once. By now his burst needs two full rotations to kill you, and inside the second you have healed a chunk back. Split-push with W, bait his E onto a non-committal angle, drop Pillar to cut the exit, finish with Chomp. Watch the ultimate timers as they rank: The Culling is 110/100/90 against Subjugate's 120/100/80, so his is back first at rank 1 and yours at rank 3. In team fights save Subjugate for an enemy frontliner.

notes: BIGGEST ADD: 'Lightslinger attacks reduce Relentless Pursuit's cooldown' is in Riot's own text and was absent from every string in both layers — while the entry's central rule, repeated six times, is to engage when that dash is down. A player counting to sixteen steps into a dash that came back early, because the empowered shots they traded through refunded it. The instruction changes from 'wait out a timer' to 'deny him empowered attacks'. SECOND ADD: Ardent Blaze is never named in either layer, yet it is the mechanic that beats Frozen Domain — it marks at 900 range and every auto into the mark gives Lucian move speed. The entry says he kites you without saying what with. CORRECTED: Subjugate was described twice as slowing Lucian. It steals Health, Armor and MR and nothing else; the slows are Chomp's and Pillar of Ice's, which matters because the whole level-6 plan was to 'lock him in place' with an ability that cannot. CORRECTED: 'two shots off every Q cast' — Lightslinger triggers off any ability including Relentless Pursuit, so his exit is also an empowered shot. Added Piercing Light's 500-range through-target behaviour, which means a minion in between is not cover against a 300-range Chomp. ADDED FOR JUNGLE: Lightslinger's second clause gives him bonus magic damage on his next two attacks when a nearby enemy champion is immobilized, so a jungler's stun feeds him — land the CC to finish the gank rather than open it. ULTIMATE TIMERS: The Culling 110/100/90 against Subjugate 120/100/80 — they cross, his first at rank 1, yours at rank 3. UNVERIFIED, LEFT ALONE: the entry says Pillar of Ice 'blocks' Relentless Pursuit mid-dash. Riot's text says Pillar becomes impassable terrain but says nothing about interrupting a dash in flight, so I kept the existing phrasing and did not strengthen it anywhere. NOT EDITED (enum): the chart gives Trundle none of seven stages in a 52.79% lane over 430 games, and win[6] reads Lucian directly above a whys[6]/spikes[3] pair saying he falls off — win[6] and phases[6].side should read Trundle. Also flagged: full phases[0].why still says Chomp 'wins almost every level-1 exchange' while content early says levels 1-3 are Lucian's; that generic line is wrong for this matchup but sits inside the length band only if replaced wholesale, and it is an argument about who wins Level 1 that the chart should settle first.
